questions.a_indistinguishability: PASS. GET /:id: get_review (1 query) then, for a foreign-named review, one in-memory Jason.decode + compare, then Response.not_found/1; a nonexistent id is 1 query then Response.not_found/1. Same status, same body and headers (same function), same DB round-trip count; the foreign branch skips get_latest_assertion_run exactly as the nonexistent branch does. /:id/context identical shape. The only delta is a microsecond-scale in-process JSON decode, not a DB-level or response-level signal. List: a hidden review is simply absent; no marker, count, or total in the page shape.
questions.b_decision_source: PASS. tenant_view/1 and TenantTarget.authorize_target_tenant/2 are unchanged and read only conn.assigns.auth_context via PlatformTenant.scope_facts_for/1 (stored flag not read). The list passes the predicate only when tenant_view != :operator; operator path passes no :row_visible? key (identical to prior behaviour). The same review_tenants_authorized?/2 backs the write routes, so read and write cannot diverge.
questions.c_cursor_count_leak: PASS. next_cursor is built only from the last EMITTED row (split_list_reviews_page on the filtered list); the between-chunk seek is a local variable never serialised. Response carries no total/count. A has-more signal is computed from visible rows only (page_size + 1 visible), so an empty next_cursor is not a hidden-row oracle. A client-forged cursor only moves the seek start and returns visible rows after that point; it discloses nothing about hidden ids/inserted_at.
questions.d_scan_cost: ACCEPTABLE (R2/R3/R7 accepted). Who can trigger: any caller holding PromotionsRead in their own tenant (TENANT-scope permission). Cost is bounded by the number of promotion_reviews in the CALLER's own schema, and a non-operator cannot create hidden rows there: submit/plan require both stored ids to be the caller's own (tenants_authorized? before any lookup, 404 otherwise), so hidden rows can only be created by platform operators acting on that tenant. The attacker therefore cannot self-inflate the scan. Work per request is sequential chunked keyset queries (index-friendly order inserted_at desc, id desc) with an in-memory decode per row; each chunk is its own short query so no long statement; memory is bounded by chunk + page_size + 1 rows. Concurrency is bounded by Plugs.Admission; per-actor rate limiting is the recorded decision 0040 (deferred to S4) and this change does not amplify request volume. Cost is incurred per request, not stored.
questions.e_malformed_legacy: PASS. Jason.decode error or a non-map JSON value (list/string/number/null) becomes %{} so both ids are nil and TenantTarget returns :not_found, i.e. hidden for non-operators, never raised; operators (platform scope) remain :ok and see them as before. Covered by tests 1(f)/1(h)/1(i) and T-11 non_map_plan_fails_closed (mutants M10/M11 killed).
questions.f_write_routes_unchanged: PASS. stored_tenants_authorized?/3 keeps the identical contract (review_not_found -> true so the downstream 404 stays byte-identical; found -> same decode-or-%{} then tenants_authorized?); the extracted review_tenants_authorized?/2 is the verbatim former body. approve_reject_stored_ids_test and the store tests were run: 55 passed across the three files (read_stored_ids, store, approve_reject_stored_ids), exit 0.

issues.title: Legacy or malformed stored plans are permanently invisible to non-operators on read routes
issues.detail: Fail-closed is the correct security posture and matches the write routes; the side effect is that a tenant admin cannot see such a row in the list or open it. Operators still can. Record as intended behaviour; no change requested.

issues.title: Pre-existing: list cursor seek decode is a bare match / String.to_integer on a client-supplied, unsigned cursor
issues.detail: decode_list_reviews_seek/1 (unchanged by this diff) can raise MatchError/ArgumentError on a hand-crafted but well-prefixed, unexpired cursor, giving a 500 (INV-8) rather than 400 invalid cursor. Not a leak and not introduced here; worth a separate issue.

issues.title: Residual timing class
issues.detail: Non-operator list latency grows with the number of hidden rows in the caller's own schema, and a foreign-named review costs one in-memory JSON decode more than a nonexistent id. Neither is byte-observable nor a cross-tenant existence oracle (the rows are in the caller's own schema; a foreign tenant's review ids are never in it). Accepted per R2/R3/R7.
